aions_core/agi_existing_models.py.why: It is the machinery that discovers Mistral/Phi-3/Bielik on the machine and keeps one loaded to generate text, not the search layer that decides what evidence to hand a model.

aions_core/aions_crla_reformed.py.why: It generates several candidate answers and runs a scored tournament to keep the winner, which is judging answer quality rather than hunting for the passages in the first place.

aions_core/aions_monitoring_dashboard.py.why: It sweeps every component for liveness and measures p95/p99 response times, which is live health and speed, not grading the correctness of one reply.

aions_core/aions_vector_enhancement.py.why: Its purpose is to give AIONS a meaning-based way to retrieve relevant material; it borrows an existing LanceDB instance rather than being the store's own service.

aions_core/tools/symbolic_probe.py.why: It walks a plain Polish sentence through Esperanto and codebook symbols to show which chunks it lands on, so it belongs with the encoding chain, not with the desktop end-to-end demos.

aions_core/tools/test_guardrail.py.why: It fires gibberish and a valid question at the server to confirm nonsense is refused, which tests trustworthiness of answers rather than whether the service is up.

control_plane/agents/__init__.py.why: It states the rule that an agent is only a declaration with an allowed-skill list and a risk ceiling, which is the permission model, not the running of skills themselves.

control_plane/models.py.why: It declares the Plan, PlanStep, ExecutionResult and ExecutionState shapes used by the command centre, so it sits with job planning rather than with the assistant's front door.

control_plane/operator/loop.py.why: It repeatedly gathers disk and service stats, restarts things with a cooldown and writes up the incident, which is self-repair rather than setting the environment up.

scripts/chatgpt_ultimate.py.why: It digs conversations, titles and account details out of another app's cache on this machine, which is intake of outside text, not a survey of drive contents.

scripts/demo_papiery.py.why: It is a runnable showcase that adds sample tasks and pops a notification to prove the flow works, rather than being the paperwork store the demo calls into.

scripts/test_llm_adapter.py.why: It confirms the local Bielik/Ollama model replies in Polish and actually used the injected context, which is about the model call working, not about the tone of a finished reply.

scripts/validate_aions_tools.py.why: It calls every MCP tool once after a code change to prove the server still exposes them, which is the connection layer rather than the health of the running services themselves.

server/app.py.why: It is the HTTP face of the vector store with session, add, search and prune endpoints, not the assistant's own question-and-answer front door.

server/store_http.py.why: Its job is holding documents in Chroma collections per session and turning distances into similarity scores, which is the embedding store rather than the plain chunk files on disk.

aions_core/PRODUCTION_AIONS_CBMS_SYSTEM..why: It chops Polish and technical words into meaningful syllables with Korean mappings and reports compression ratios, which is the encoding scheme, not the model-hosting machinery it happens to use.

aions_core/agi_evolution.py.why: It watches performance across eight abilities over time and proposes improvement strategies, which is long-term self-improvement rather than grading one answer.

aions_core/agi_neural_backprop.py.why: It is the trainable engine that adjusts itself from feedback gradients across multi-hop reasoning, so it is self-improvement rather than the retrieval it reasons over.

aions_core/api.py.why: It is the HTTP entry point that hands incoming questions to the assembled AIONS core, not the vector-store service that keeps documents.

aions_core/server/stylist.py.why: It only reshapes spacing and paragraphing of an already-settled answer while confirming no numbers or citations vanished, so it is presentation rather than factual grounding.

aions_core/server/ts_symbols.py.why: It parses source files to list every function and class with its line numbers and callers, which is surveying code structure rather than the bookkeeping of the knowledge folders.

aions_core/smart_cbms.py.why: Its whole point is deciding whether the cached retrieval is good enough or a bigger model must be paid for, which is the search-and-escalate decision, not the model-loading machinery.

aions_core/tools/rebuild_manifest_force..why: It walks the chunk files on disk and rewrites the manifest index, which is housekeeping of the plain stored pieces rather than any similarity database.

control_plane/node_registry.py.why: It keeps the roll of worker machines with their tools, health and load so work can be routed, which is fleet bookkeeping rather than permission checking.

control_plane/skills/planner.py.why: It looks for a cached recipe or candidate skills for an intent from the skill registry, rather than breaking a goal into numbered steps and choosing a machine to run them.

mcpServers/VS_CODE_MCP_CODEX/src/filesys.why: It keeps a JSON list of every file with size and date so name searches skip walking the disk, which is the quick file finder, not the deep dependency scan of a codebase.

scripts/aions_python.sh.why: It pins every script to the same venv and Python version, creating it if missing, which is groundwork before anything runs rather than a health check on live services.

scripts/ingest_treasures_tier2.py.why: It is a loading job that pushes catalogue summaries into Chroma collections, not the drive survey that produced the catalogue in the first place.

scripts/verify_tier1_chroma.py.why: It runs sample searches and document counts after an ingest to confirm the right material landed in Chroma, so it checks the store rather than the quality of any answer.

server/__init__.py.why: It is only the package marker for the vector-store service directory, declaring importability rather than doing any storing or searching itself.
